name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Indonesia's rupiah hit record lows near 18,290 per dollar on 16–17 Nov; no EM default or IMF rescue
state: Indonesia's rupiah hit record lows near 18,280–18,290 per dollar on 16–17 Nov amid political uncertainty after the vice-president's resignation and expectations of a rate rise, about 1.6% weaker than near 18,000 on 21 Oct (Trading Economics). The Turkish lira has traded near a record of about 50 per dollar since 3 Nov (Trading Economics). Neither has fallen 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy in default, under capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 17 Nov.
for_you: A weaker rupiah raises import costs in Indonesia. Travellers and firms with costs in these currencies are most exposed to further swings.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major EM currency down >10% in a month, no default, capital controls or emergency IMF request

sources.title: Rupiah Hovers Near IDR 18,000 as BI Adjusts Policy Tools (news stream)
Turkish Lira Holds at Record Lows

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
